solution: For stretched or compressed wire \[R \propto l^{2}\] \[\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}} = \frac{l_{1}^{2}}{l_{2}^{2}}\] \[\Rightarrow \frac{R}{R_{2}} = \frac{l^{2}}{(1.25l)^{2}}\] \[\Rightarrow R_{2} = 1.5625R\] \(\%\) increase \(\rightarrow 56.25\% \approx 56\%\)
note: length l was printed as I and 1.25l as 1.251; 1.5625 is a 56.25% rise

solution: Let each resistance be \(R_{0}\) at \(0^{\circ}C\), so \(R_{1}=R_{0}(1+\alpha_{1}t)\) and \(R_{2}=R_{0}(1+\alpha_{2}t)\). In series \[R_{s}=2R_{0}\left(1+\frac{\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}}{2}t\right)\quad\Rightarrow\quad \alpha_{s}=\frac{\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}}{2}.\] In parallel, to first order in the small quantities \(\alpha t\), \[R_{p}=\frac{R_{1}R_{2}}{R_{1}+R_{2}}=\frac{R_{0}\left(1+\alpha_{1}t\right)\left(1+\alpha_{2}t\right)}{2+\left(\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}\right)t}\approx\frac{R_{0}}{2}\left[1+\left(\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}\right)t\right]\left[1-\frac{\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}}{2}t\right]\approx\frac{R_{0}}{2}\left(1+\frac{\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}}{2}t\right),\] so \(\alpha_{p}=\dfrac{\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}}{2}\) as well. Numerical cross-check with \(R_{0}=1,\ \alpha_{1}=0.001,\ \alpha_{2}=0.003,\ t=10\): \(R_{1}=1.01,\ R_{2}=1.03\); parallel value \(=0.50995\) against \(0.5\) at \(0^{\circ}C\), a fractional rise of \(0.0199\), i.e. \(\alpha_{p}\approx0.00199\), matching \(\left(\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}\right)/2=0.002\). Hence the correct choice is B.
